physicalNotes: Radius 0.19448691 Jupiter radii from Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..56S/abstract): 13,904.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.02108056 Jupiter masses (Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..56S/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SUAREZ_MASCARENO_ET_AL_2024): P 8.465651 d
sources.shape: Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SUAREZ_MASCARENO_ET_AL_2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0749 au and stellar radius 0.733 solar radii; Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SUAREZ_MASCARENO_ET_AL_2024): inclination 87.938 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Suárez Mascareño et al. 2024 (2024A&A...685A..56S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SUAREZ_MASCARENO_ET_AL_2024): transit mid-time 2460204.9675 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 9 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
